answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it may trade, then slash that stake when independent audits prove it coordinated duplicate accounts to claim the same reward. A public mirror of signed trades lets auditors connect the accounts, while a cipher commits to each claim before outcomes are known, preventing a late switch. The attacker must fund every identity and risks losing those funds, so multiplying fake accounts becomes costly rather than free. The ivory token is only a receipt for the locked stake, not a substitute for it.
